changesets.summary: The branch store's branches are now `thunderjar/capture/<session>`, not `thunderjar-capture/<session>`. Branches under the old name are no longer read: rename one to keep it, e.g. `git branch -m thunderjar-capture/<session> thunderjar/capture/<session>`.
Add `capture pull`, which fetches the captures from a remote. `capture push --fetch` still works, but is no longer in the help.
`init` scaffolds `.thunderjar/AGENTS.md`, with the defaults an agent uses when it writes a new test case.

Give measurement containers a run's secret environment variables: its test case's `secretEnv` and its harness's `requiredEnv`. Each is passed by name, as to the agent's container, so its value comes from the shell that runs Thunderjar, or a runtime's runner, and is never on a command line, in a log or in an image. A `shell` measurement can now use, e.g., `DATABASE_URL`. The test case's `env` already reached them, through the postrun image.

Add `thunderjar purge image`, which deletes the images executions left, from the local Docker daemon and the image store, and records each postrun image purged on its container run. Choose executions by ID, `--test-case` or `--all`, narrowed with `--older-than`, and prerun images with `--kind prerun`. It says what it would purge and asks first; `--yes` skips the question, `--dry-run` only prints, and `--record-only` marks images removed some other way. The image store is purged through the registry's standard API, or, where the registry refuses deletes, by the new `imageStore.deleteCommand`. `show` lists an execution's purged runs below its table, and a container run's purge beside its postrun image; `--json` and `view`'s API include it. A purged run's measures still count.
With an image store, a container run records, and `show` prints, the pushed registry reference of its postrun image, not its local name.

A harness's `requiredEnv` can name any one of several variables, `{ oneOf: ["A", "B"] }`: the first that's set is passed to the agent, and only it, and the run's record (`harnessEnv`) and `show` name it. `claudeCode()` now needs `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, a subscription token from `claude setup-token`, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and passes the token if both are set. Its harnesses' permutation hashes change, so their prerun images are rebuilt once.
A container run's duration is never negative, even if the clock is set back while it runs.

Postrun images no longer hold the values of the environment variables an agent ran with.

`docker commit` saved the agent container's whole environment into the postrun image's config, including each harness's `requiredEnv`, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and anything a base image's `runOptions` passed with `-e` or `--env-file`. Now, when the container is committed, every variable its prerun image doesn't set is blanked, and every one it does set gets the prerun image's value back.

**If you ran earlier versions:** their postrun images hold the values of the variables passed to the agent. Rotate those keys, and delete those images, locally and from any registry they were pushed to.

Measurement containers start from the postrun image, so they no longer see those variables either. A later change will pass them in where measurements need them.

Look for a run's secrets in the files of its postrun image before it's pushed. The agent, or what it runs, can write a key into a file, e.g. a log line, a `.env` or a session file, which would be committed and pushed with the image. So once each container run is committed, a short-lived container from its postrun image is given the run's secret variables by name, its harness's `requiredEnv` and its test case's `secretEnv`, and searches its files for their values, skipping `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev` and other mounts. The values never leave Docker: only the names found, and the paths of the files holding them, are recorded with the run, as `secretsFound`.

`run` and `attach` warn of each as they finish, and `show` and `--json` say so. The run is only flagged: its image is still committed, measured and pushed, so treat a secret found in a pushed image as exposed, and rotate it.

Values shorter than 12 characters, or on more than one line, aren't searched for. A search that fails, or takes longer than `THUNDERJAR_SECRET_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (120 by default), doesn't fail the run: it's recorded as `secretSearchFailed`, with why, and `run` and `show` say so.

`thunderjar capture` can keep each session on a branch, `thunderjar-capture/<session>`, for remotes that take only branches: set `THUNDERJAR_CAPTURE_STORE=branch`, the default in Claude Code cloud sessions. `capture list` and `capture push` read both stores, and `capture import` copies branch captures into `refs/thunderjar/capture/`.
Add `thunderjar capture`: record every coding-agent session as git refs, for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and OpenCode.
